statement: Wisp must assemble a bounded, read-only implementation context from an explicitly selected plan batch or task and its verified governing spec.
stakeholder: A developer or coding-agent harness preparing an implementation session.
why: Callers repeatedly load and reconcile plans and specs by hand, which spends agent context on deterministic checks and can pass stale or mismatched instructions into implementation.
done_when: A caller can select exactly one declared batch or task from an explicit plan path.
Wisp verifies the plan and governing spec contracts, identities, paths, criterion mappings, and raw-byte spec hash before returning context.
The result contains the exact selected implementation steps and governing criteria with source digests and explicit gaps, without private reasoning or inferred approval.
Unsafe paths, stale or inconsistent artifacts, invalid selections, changed inputs, and oversized required context produce typed failures without a partial success result.
The operation does not modify canonical artifacts, Git state, or derived state and does not execute commands found in a plan.
The versioned result can be consumed without assuming that it is approval, current code evidence, or proof that declared files cover all affected code.
Smith can optionally consume a valid Wisp result while preserving each harness's existing behavior when Wisp is unavailable or rejects the handoff.
out_of_scope: Monokl code evidence, SQLite, caches, watchers, MCP, embeddings, or model-generated summaries.
Automatic batch scheduling, prerequisite completion inference, command execution, approval, commits, or artifact repair.
Changing Claude/AGY or Codex spec-drift policy, making Wisp a required runtime dependency, or claiming task outcomes or reduced context cost without a controlled evaluation.
